title: Multiples, Factors, Prime Numbers, LCM and HCF
seo_title: Grade 6 Multiples, Factors and Primes Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Multiples of 2-digit and 3-digit whole numbers; factors of 2-digit and 3-digit whole numbers; prime factors of numbers to at least 100; prime numbers to at least 100; LCM and HCF of numbers to at least 3-digit whole numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 worksheets: factors, multiples, prime numbers, factor trees, HCF and LCM. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: A prime has exactly two factors.
key_sub: HCF: biggest shared factor. LCM: smallest shared multiple.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself (2, 3, 5, 7, 11 …). 1 is not prime.
  • A composite number has more than two factors.
  • The HCF is the biggest factor two numbers share. The LCM is the smallest multiple they share.
  • A factor tree breaks a number into prime factors: 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3.

Examples

Example

HCF and LCM of 12 and 18

factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12

multiples: 36 is first in both lists

Answer: HCF 6, LCM 36

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
1 is prime1 has only one factor.
HCF or LCM?Factors are small; multiples are big.
Multiplying for the LCM12 × 18 = 216 is common, but not the lowest.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about multiples and factors?
faq.a: Find multiples and factors of numbers to at least 100, prime numbers to at least 100, and the LCM and HCF of whole numbers.
To find a common denominator for fractions.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 18?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Do not forget 1 and 18, and do not miss 3 × 6. 18, 36, 54, 72 are multiples of 18, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 28?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 28, 2 × 14, 4 × 7. So the factors are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. Do not forget 1 and 28, and do not miss 4 × 7. 28, 56, 84, 112 are multiples of 28, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 36?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9, 6 × 6. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Do not forget 1 and 36, and do not miss 4 × 9. 36, 72, 108, 144 are multiples of 36, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 40?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 40, 2 × 20, 4 × 10, 5 × 8. So the factors are 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Do not forget 1 and 40, and do not miss 5 × 8. 40, 80, 120, 160 are multiples of 40, not factors.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 48?
Which number is not a factor of 60?
Which number is not a factor of 72?
Which number is not a factor of 90?
Which number is a factor of 84?
items.e: 14 × 6 = 84, so 14 is a factor of 84. 168 is a multiple of 84, not a factor, and 16 and 24 leave a remainder.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 96?
items.e: 32 × 3 = 96, so 32 is a factor of 96. 192 is a multiple of 96, not a factor, and 36 and 28 leave a remainder.

items.q: How many factor pairs does 36 have?
items.e: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9 and 6 × 6. That is 5 factor pairs. 6 × 6 counts as a pair, and 9 is the number of factors, not pairs.

items.q: Thabo lists the factor pairs of 72: 1 × 72, 2 × 36, 3 × 24, 6 × 12, 8 × 9. Which pair did he miss?
items.e: Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. 72 ÷ 4 = 18, so 4 × 18 is missing. 9 × 8 is the same pair as 8 × 9, and 7 × 10 and 5 × 14 both make 70, not 72.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 7?
items.e: 7 × 9 = 63, so 63 is a multiple of 7. 27 ÷ 7 = 3 R6. 17 ÷ 7 = 2 R3. 57 ÷ 7 = 8 R1. Having a 7 as a digit does not make a number a multiple of 7.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 8?
items.e: 8 × 12 = 96, so 96 is a multiple of 8. 58 ÷ 8 = 7 R2. 18 ÷ 8 = 2 R2. 84 ÷ 8 = 10 R4. 84 is a multiple of 4 and of 12, but not of 8.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 9?
Which number is not a multiple of 6?
items.e: Multiples of 6 are even. 63 is odd, so 63 is not a multiple of 6 (it is a multiple of 3, 7 and 9). 6 × 7 = 42, 6 × 9 = 54 and 6 × 12 = 72.

items.q: What is the 12th multiple of 7?
items.e: The 12th multiple of 7 is 7 × 12 = 84. 77 is the 11th multiple, 91 is the 13th, and 19 is 7 + 12.

items.q: Which list shows the first five multiples of 6?
items.e: The multiples of 6 are 6 × 1, 6 × 2, 6 × 3 …: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. The first multiple is 6 itself. 1, 2, 3, 6 are the factors of 6.

items.q: Andile says 4 is a multiple of 12. Is he right?
items.e: 4 × 3 = 12, so 4 is a factor of 12 and 12 is a multiple of 4. A factor divides the number; a multiple is the number times 1, 2, 3 … 4 is not prime: 4 = 2 × 2.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 9 × 4 = 36, so 36 is a multiple of 9 (and 9 is a factor of 36). 36 ÷ 8 = 4 R4, so 8 is not a factor of 36.

items.q: Which of these is a prime number?
items.e: 23 has exactly two factors, 1 and 23, so 23 is prime. 21 = 3 × 7, so 21 is not prime. 27 = 3 × 9, so 27 is not prime. 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime.

items.q: Which number is not a prime number?
items.e: 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime. 2, 3 and 5 are prime: each has exactly two factors. 2 is prime, even though it is even.

items.q: Which shows 24 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3. 4 × 6 is not finished, because 4 and 6 are not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written.

items.q: Which shows 60 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5. 6 × 10 is not finished, because 6 and 10 are not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written.

items.q: Which shows 45 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 45 = 3 × 3 × 5. 5 × 9 is not finished, because 9 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written.

items.q: What are the prime factors of 30?
items.e: 30 = 2 × 3 × 5, and 2, 3 and 5 are all prime. So the prime factors are 2, 3 and 5. 1 is not prime, 6 = 2 × 3 and 15 = 3 × 5.

items.q: How many prime numbers are there between 10 and 20?
items.e: The primes are 11, 13, 17 and 19: 4 primes. 15 is odd but not prime (15 = 3 × 5).

items.q: Lethabo says 1 is a prime number. Is he right?
items.e: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime. It is not composite either.

items.q: Nomsa says 2 is not a prime number because it is even. Is she right?
items.e: The factors of 2 are 1 and 2, so 2 is prime. It is the only even prime: every other even number can be divided by 2.

items.q: Which of these is a square number?
items.e: 7 × 7 = 49, so 49 is a square number. 14 is 7 × 2, 27 is a cube number (3 × 3 × 3), and 50 is between 7 × 7 and 8 × 8.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 12?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Do not forget 1 and 12, and do not miss 3 × 4. 12, 24, 36, 48 are multiples of 12, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 20?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 20, 2 × 10, 4 × 5. So the factors are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Do not forget 1 and 20, and do not miss 4 × 5. 20, 40, 60, 80 are multiples of 20, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 30?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 30, 2 × 15, 3 × 10, 5 × 6. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Do not forget 1 and 30, and do not miss 5 × 6. 30, 60, 90, 120 are multiples of 30, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 42?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 42, 2 × 21, 3 × 14, 6 × 7. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42. Do not forget 1 and 42, and do not miss 6 × 7. 42, 84, 126, 168 are multiples of 42, not factors.

items.q: Is 1 a prime number, a composite number or neither?
items.e: A prime number has exactly two factors. A composite number has more than two. 1 has only one factor (itself), so it is neither prime nor composite.

items.q: Fatima says 2 is a composite number because it is even. Is she right?
items.e: The factors of 2 are 1 and 2: exactly two factors, so 2 is prime. It is the only even prime. Every other even number has 2 as a factor as well, so it is composite.

items.q: Which of these is a composite number?
items.e: 9 = 3 × 3, so 9 has more than two factors (1, 3, 9). It is composite. 2 and 7 are prime: each has exactly two factors. 1 is neither prime nor composite.

items.q: Which list shows only prime numbers?
items.e: 2, 3, 5 and 7 each have exactly two factors, so 2, 3, 5, 7 are all prime. 1 is not prime, 9 = 3 × 3 and 15 = 3 × 5.

items.q: How many prime numbers are there from 1 to 20?
items.e: The primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19: 8 primes. 9 comes from counting 1, 7 from leaving out 2, and 10 is the number of odd numbers (9 and 15 are odd but not prime).

items.q: How many factors does 16 have?
items.e: The factor pairs are 1 × 16, 2 × 8 and 4 × 4. The factors are 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16: 5 factors. Count 4 only once (6 counts it twice), 3 is the number of factor pairs, and 8 is half of 16.

items.q: What is the prime factorization of 24?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3. 4 × 6 is not finished, because 4 and 6 are not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. Write a repeated prime every time it appears.

items.q: What is the prime factorization of 60?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5. 6 × 10 is not finished, because 6 and 10 are not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. Write a repeated prime every time it appears.

items.q: What is the prime factorization of 45?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 45 = 3 × 3 × 5. 5 × 9 is not finished, because 9 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. Write a repeated prime every time it appears.

items.q: What is the prime factorization of 36?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. 6 × 6 is not finished, because 6 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. Write a repeated prime every time it appears.

items.q: What is the prime factorization of 72?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. 8 × 9 is not finished, because 8 and 9 are not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. Write a repeated prime every time it appears.

items.q: What is the prime factorization of 90?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 90 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 5. 9 × 10 is not finished, because 9 and 10 are not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. Write a repeated prime every time it appears.

items.q: What number is missing from the factor tree?
items.e: The branches of 84 must multiply to 84: 4 × ? = 84, so ? = 84 ÷ 4 = 21. Check: 21 = 3 × 7. 80 comes from subtracting 4, 88 from adding 4, and 42 is 84 ÷ 2.

items.q: What number is at the top of the factor tree?
items.e: Multiply the primes at the ends: 2 × 5 × 3 × 5 = 150. Or 10 × 15 = 150. 17 comes from adding 2 + 5 + 3 + 5, 30 uses each prime only once, and 75 leaves out the 2.

items.q: What number is missing from the factor tree?
items.e: 2 × ? = 98, so ? = 98 ÷ 2 = 49, and 49 = 7 × 7. 14 is 7 + 7, 96 comes from subtracting 2, and 196 comes from multiplying 98 × 2.

items.q: What is the prime factorization of 18?
items.e: Split 18 into a factor pair and keep going until every factor is prime: 18 = 3 × 6 = 2 × 3 × 3. 3 × 6 is not finished, because 6 is not prime. Write every prime, even when it repeats, and do not write 1.

items.q: Which shows 12 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3. 3 × 4 is not finished, because 4 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 2 × 3 leaves out a repeated prime: 2 × 3 = 6.

items.q: Which shows 18 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 18 = 2 × 3 × 3. 3 × 6 is not finished, because 6 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 2 × 3 leaves out a repeated prime: 2 × 3 = 6.

items.q: Which shows 20 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 20 = 2 × 2 × 5. 4 × 5 is not finished, because 4 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 2 × 5 leaves out a repeated prime: 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q: Which shows 40 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 40 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5. 5 × 8 is not finished, because 8 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 2 × 5 leaves out a repeated prime: 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q: Which shows 63 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 63 = 3 × 3 × 7. 7 × 9 is not finished, because 9 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 3 × 7 leaves out a repeated prime: 3 × 7 = 21.

items.q: Which shows 75 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 75 = 3 × 5 × 5. 5 × 15 is not finished, because 15 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 3 × 5 leaves out a repeated prime: 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: What number is missing from the factor tree?
items.e: The two branches multiply to make 48. 6 × ? = 48, and 6 × 8 = 48, so the missing number is 8. Check: 8 = 2 × 4. 42 is 48 − 6, 54 is 48 + 6, and 288 is 48 × 6.

items.q: What number is missing from the factor tree?
items.e: 10 splits into 2 × ?. 2 × 5 = 10, so the missing number is 5. 8 is 10 − 2, 12 is 10 + 2 and 20 is 10 × 2. So 90 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 5.

items.q: What number is at the top of the factor tree?
items.e: The top number is 8 × 9 = 72. Check: 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 72. 17 is 8 + 9, 89 is just 8 and 9 written side by side, and 63 is 7 × 9.

items.q: Which number is 2 × 2 × 3 × 5?
items.e: 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 3 = 12, 12 × 5 = 60. 12 comes from adding (2 + 2 + 3 + 5), 30 from using only one 2, and 120 from using three 2s.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 12 and 18?
items.e: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6. The highest is 6. Keep 1 and the highest common factor in the list, and use only numbers that divide both.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 16 and 40?
items.e: Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Common factors: 1, 2, 4, 8. The highest is 8. Keep 1 and the highest common factor in the list, and use only numbers that divide both.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 24 and 36?
items.e: Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The highest is 12. Keep 1 and the highest common factor in the list, and use only numbers that divide both.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 36 and 54?
items.e: 9 × 4 = 36 and 9 × 6 = 54, so 9 is a common factor. 4 is a factor of 36 only, 27 is a factor of 54 only, and 108 is a common multiple.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 42 and 60?
items.e: 6 × 7 = 42 and 6 × 10 = 60, so 6 is a common factor. 7 is a factor of 42 only, 10 is a factor of 60 only, and 420 is a common multiple.

items.q: Which number is not a common factor of 48 and 80?
items.e: 6 is a factor of 48, but 80 ÷ 6 = 13 remainder 2, so 6 is not a common factor. 2, 8 and 16 divide both numbers.

items.q: Which number is not a common factor of 60 and 90?
items.e: 4 is a factor of 60, but 90 ÷ 4 = 22 remainder 2, so 4 is not a common factor. 5, 6 and 15 divide both numbers.

items.q: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 14 and 21?
items.e: Factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14. Factors of 21: 1, 3, 7, 21. Common factors: 1, 7. The highest is 7. 2 is a factor of 14 only, so it is not a common factor.

items.q: What is the HCF of 20 and 30?
items.e: Factors of 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Common factors: 1, 2, 5, 10. The highest is 10. 5 is a common factor too, but not the highest.

items.q: What is the HCF of 18 and 27?
items.e: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 27: 1, 3, 9, 27. Common factors: 1, 3, 9. The highest is 9. 3 is a common factor too, but not the highest.

items.q: Which list shows the first 3 common multiples of 4 and 6?
items.e: Multiples of 6: 6, 12. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12. The first number in both lists is 12. The common multiples are the multiples of the LCM: 12, 24, 36. Counting in 4 × 6 = 24s skips 12.

items.q: Which list shows the first 3 common multiples of 6 and 9?
items.e: Multiples of 9: 9, 18. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18. The first number in both lists is 18. The common multiples are the multiples of the LCM: 18, 36, 54. Counting in 6 × 9 = 54s skips 18.

items.q: Which list shows the first 3 common multiples of 10 and 12?
items.e: Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60. Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. The first number in both lists is 60. The common multiples are the multiples of the LCM: 60, 120, 180. Counting in 10 × 12 = 120s skips 60.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 3 and 4?
items.e: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12. Multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12. The first number in both lists is 12. 3 and 4 share no factor except 1, so here the LCM is 3 × 4.

items.q: What is the LCM of 4 and 8?
items.e: Multiples of 8: 8. Multiples of 4: 4, 8. The first number in both lists is 8. 8 is a multiple of 4, so the bigger number is the LCM.

items.q: What is the LCM of 4 and 10?
items.e: Multiples of 10: 10, 20. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. The first number in both lists is 20. 4 × 10 = 40 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.

items.q: What is the LCM of 6 and 10?
items.e: Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. The first number in both lists is 30. 6 × 10 = 60 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.

items.q: What is the LCM of 5 and 7?
items.e: Multiples of 7: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35. Multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. The first number in both lists is 35. 5 and 7 share no factor except 1, so here the LCM is 5 × 7.

items.q: What is the LCM of 8 and 10?
items.e: Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40. The first number in both lists is 40. 8 × 10 = 80 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.

items.q: What is the LCM of 9 and 12?
items.e: Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36. Multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36. The first number in both lists is 36. 9 × 12 = 108 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.

items.q: I am a prime number between 40 and 50. The digits of my number add up to 7. What number am I?
items.e: The primes between 40 and 50 are 41, 43 and 47. 4 + 3 = 7, so the number is 43. 49 is not prime: 49 = 7 × 7.

items.q: I am a square number less than 50. I am also a multiple of 6. What number am I?
items.e: The square numbers less than 50 are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36 and 49. Only 36 is a multiple of 6 (6 × 6 = 36). 16 is square but not a multiple of 6, and 24 and 18 are multiples of 6 but not square.

items.q: I am an odd cube number between 20 and 100. What number am I?
items.e: The cube numbers between 20 and 100 are 27 (3 × 3 × 3) and 64 (4 × 4 × 4). 64 is even, so the number is 27. 25 and 81 are square numbers, not cube numbers.

items.q: Karabo thinks of a number between 10 and 20. It is a factor of 36 and a multiple of 4. What is her number?
items.e: Factors of 36 between 10 and 20: 12 and 18. Only 12 is a multiple of 4, so the number is 12. 18 is a factor of 36 but not a multiple of 4, and 16 is a multiple of 4 but not a factor of 36.

items.q: What is the total of all the prime numbers between 20 and 30?
items.e: The primes between 20 and 30 are 23 and 29. 23 + 29 = 52. 21 = 3 × 7, 25 = 5 × 5 and 27 = 3 × 9 are odd, but not prime. 100 is 21 + 23 + 27 + 29.

items.q: Which pair of prime numbers has a total of 24?
items.e: 11 and 13 are both prime, and 11 + 13 = 24. 9 and 15 are not prime, 1 is not prime, and 22 = 2 × 11 is not prime.

items.q: Aisha has 24 pencils and 36 rubbers. She wants to make identical packs with nothing left over. What is the greatest number of packs she can make?
items.e: Find the HCF of 24 and 36. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The HCF is 12, so she can make 12 packs, each with 2 pencils and 3 rubbers. 6 packs would work too, but 12 is greater. 72 is the LCM.

items.q: Refilwe has two ribbons, 48 cm and 60 cm long. She cuts both into pieces that are all the same length, with nothing left over. What is the longest each piece can be?
items.e: The length must divide both 48 and 60. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The HCF is 12 cm: 4 pieces from the first ribbon and 5 from the second. 240 is the LCM, longer than both ribbons.

items.q: A PE teacher has 18 boys and 27 girls. Every team must have the same number of boys and the same number of girls, with no one left out. What is the greatest number of teams?
items.e: Find the HCF of 18 and 27. Common factors: 1, 3, 9. The HCF is 9, so there are 9 teams, each with 2 boys and 3 girls. 45 is 18 + 27, the number of children.

items.q: Sibusiso cuts a piece of card 30 cm by 42 cm into equal squares, as large as possible, with none left over. What is the side length of each square?
items.e: The side must divide both 30 and 42. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6. The HCF is 6 cm, which gives 5 rows of 7 squares. 210 is the LCM, and it is bigger than the card.

items.q: Siyabonga sets up 36 chairs for the school assembly in equal rows. Which arrangement uses all 36 chairs?
A teacher puts 28 chairs in equal rows, with at least 2 rows and at least 2 chairs in each row. 4 rows of 7 and 7 rows of 4 count as different. How many arrangements are possible?
items.e: The number of rows must be a factor of 28 between 2 and 14: 2, 4, 7 and 14. That gives 4 arrangements: 2 × 14, 4 × 7, 7 × 4 and 14 × 2. 6 would include 1 row of 28 and 28 rows of 1.

items.q: Ms. Chen has 23 chairs. She cannot set them in equal rows, unless she uses 1 row. Why?
items.e: The only factors of 23 are 1 and 23, so 23 is prime: the only rows are 1 row of 23 or 23 rows of 1. Being odd is not the reason: 21 chairs can make 3 rows of 7.

items.q: The gym has 120 chairs for the Grade 6 graduation. They go in equal rows, with between 10 and 20 rows. Which number of rows works?
items.e: 120 ÷ 12 = 10, so 12 rows of 10 chairs works. 120 ÷ 14, 120 ÷ 16 and 120 ÷ 18 all leave a remainder. Being even is not enough.

items.q: Which number of chairs can be set out in rows of 3, in rows of 4 or in rows of 6, with no chairs left over?
items.e: 36 ÷ 3 = 12, 36 ÷ 4 = 9 and 36 ÷ 6 = 6, so 36 works. 30 and 42 are not divisible by 4 (30 ÷ 4 = 7 R2, 42 ÷ 4 = 10 R2), and 2 + 6 = 8, so 26 is not divisible by 3.

items.q: A bakery packs 132 butter tarts in boxes of 6. Will any tarts be left over?
c: No. All even numbers divide by 6
items.e: 132 is even, and 1 + 3 + 2 = 6 is divisible by 3. So 132 is divisible by 6: 132 ÷ 6 = 22 boxes, with none left over. Not every even number works: 140 ÷ 6 has a remainder.

items.q: A farm packs 1 318 eggs in trays of 4. How many eggs are left over?
items.e: The last two digits make 18. 18 ÷ 4 = 4 R2, so 1 318 ÷ 4 = 329 R2: 2 eggs are left over. 1 318 is even, but that does not make it divisible by 4.

items.q: Juice boxes come in packs of 8. Which order of juice boxes can be packed with none left over?
items.e: 2 136: the last three digits make 136, and 136 ÷ 8 = 17, so it is divisible by 8. 2 124, 2 140 and 2 116 are divisible by 4, but their last three digits (124, 140, 116) are not divisible by 8. 24 is divisible by 8, but 124 is not.

items.q: Ofentse packs 72 granola bars into equal bags for a field trip. Which number of bags does not work?
items.e: 72 ends in 2, so it is not divisible by 5: 5 bags do not work. 72 ÷ 8 = 9, 72 ÷ 9 = 8 and 72 ÷ 6 = 12.

items.q: A box holds 30 chocolates in equal rows. Which number of rows is not possible?
items.e: 30 ÷ 4 = 7 R2, so 4 rows is not possible. 5 rows of 6, 3 rows of 10 and 2 rows of 15 all make 30. 4 is even like 30, but it is not a factor of 30.
